:::{#def-result}
#### Result

A **result** is a proposition (@def-proposition)
that has a proof (@def-proof).
These notes label each result by its role:
as a theorem (@def-theorem), a lemma (@def-lemma), or a corollary (@def-corollary).

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-theorem}
#### Theorem

A **theorem** is a result (@def-result) of interest in its own right.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-lemma}
#### Lemma

A **lemma** is a result (@def-result) proved mainly as a step in the proof of another result.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-corollary}
#### Corollary

A **corollary** is a result (@def-result) that follows from a theorem
with little extra work.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#rem-proposition-as-result}
#### "Proposition" as a kind of result

Some sources also call a result of moderate importance a "proposition".
In these notes, "proposition" always means a sentence that is true or false
(@def-proposition), whether or not it has been proved.

:::
